simple.meaning: קְטַר (qᵉṭar) is a Hebrew object word meaning “a knot (as tied up), i.e. (figuratively) a riddle ; also a vertebra (as if a knot).” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Daniel 5:6. The surrounding context includes kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to קְטַר (H7001) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.

definitions.full: H7001. qetar [ קְטַר ] noun masculine Dan 5:6 joint, knot ; — literal plural construct קִטְרֵי 5:6 joints of his loin; figurative absolute קִטְרִין 5:12 ; 5:16 , usually knotty things , difficulties (Syriac PS 3591 ); but probably of magic spells, banns (also Syriac PS l.c. , compare Brock 319b ), so Bev, see also Dr.
